title: Cross-Entropy & Log Loss
interviewAnswer: Cross-entropy evaluates a predicted probability distribution against the target. In classification it rewards high probability on the true class and heavily penalizes confident wrong predictions.
why: Cross-entropy is a core training objective in classification and language modeling.
intuition: Predicting 0.9 for the correct class is mildly penalized; predicting 0.001 is punished strongly because -log(0.001) is large.
deepDive: With one-hot targets, cross-entropy is the negative log probability assigned to the true class and corresponds to maximum likelihood for common probabilistic classifiers.
commonMistakes: Applying softmax twice when a framework loss expects logits.
production: Monitor calibration and downstream decision metrics in addition to cross-entropy.
workedExample: True-class probability .9 gives loss ≈.105; probability .1 gives ≈2.303.
